title: Comparison of patient simulation techniques in the psychotherapeutic field for training diagnostics and interviewing - how realistic is ChatGPT as a patient?
summary:
The aim of this study is to investigate the use and evaluation of training material in the form of a role script for a mentally ill patient. The focus is on the evaluation of the use of a virtual patient (VP) based on artificial intelligence (AI) compared to a simulated standardized patient (SSP).  

Background: In the training of psychotherapists, SSPs are used as standard to teach conversation techniques and diagnostic skills. Although this teaching format is effective, it has some practical disadvantages: Preparing and training SSPs is time-consuming, their availability is limited, and their use in courses is therefore often difficult to plan. In addition, each session requires a significant amount of personnel and financial resources. Recently, artificial intelligence has been increasingly used as an alternative to human SSPs in the medical and nursing fields. Such computer-generated patients are referred to as virtual patients (VPs) and can appear in various formats—for example, as text-based chatbots or avatar-based simulations that also reproduce facial expressions, voice, and eye contact. Initial studies show promising results in terms of satisfaction, applicability, and user experience when using these systems (Hossain, Kelson & Morrison, 2024; Chen et al., 2024; Ryu et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024). Research on avatar-based VPs also suggests that audiovisual, nonverbal signals can contribute to greater social presence and more realistic interaction (Mavrogiorgou et al., 2024; Graf et al., 2024). However, little is known about whether such VP formats can also convincingly represent complex mental disorders and how they compare to SSPs in terms of realism and learning effectiveness. The present study aims to contribute to investigating these open questions.

Hypotheses: We expect greater consistency in the avatar and ChatGPT conditions than in the SSP conditions with regard to the variability of the core symptoms reproduced by the VP. We also expect a better rating for the avatar and ChatGPT conditions in terms of application and usability, especially in the text version. At the same time, we expect less realism in the ChatGPT condition compared to the conditions with a real actor on site.   For the avatar, we expect realism that is higher than that of ChatGPT but lower than that of an SSP. We do not expect any differences between an actor in telephone or text contact and within the ChatGPT versions. 

Subjects: Psychology students and individuals in psychotherapy training will be recruited as study participants.

Study procedure: Participants are assigned to one of six experimental conditions. In each condition, they conduct a conversation with a simulated, fictitious patient, either in writing or orally, depending on the format. Depending on the condition, this patient is represented either by a human actor or a virtual patient. The underlying role script describes a 35-year-old man with narcissistic personality disorder who has developed depressive symptoms after losing his job and is now presenting for an initial consultation. Participants are asked to conduct a diagnostic interview with the patient.
Afterwards, they answer questions about the user-friendliness and applicability of the respective format, the perceived realism, and how clearly and authentically the patient portrayal conveyed the relevant information.
conditions: No illness or health problem is being investigated. The focus is on improving the training of psychotherapists.

interventions.name: Intervention group1: Case presentation by a trained acting patient in presence (1 Session à 20min)
Intervention group2: Case presentation by a trained acting patient via telephone contact/ audio-only version (1 Session à 20min)
Intervention group3: Case presentation by a trained acting patient via text chat (1 Session à 20min)
Intervention group4: Case presentation by ChatGPT using the text function (chat history) (1 Session à 20min)
Intervention group5: Case presentation by ChatGPT with the help of the voice function (verbal exchange) (1 Session à 20min)
Intervention group 6: Case presentation by a virtual avatar via the AI “Wonda” (verbal exchange) (1 session à 20 min)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Students or trainees as psychotherapists
Fluent German skills (spoken and written)
Exclusion criteria:
Non
